data.narrative:
Dendra Systems is a Series A climate & energy company that has raised $18M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a broader Climate & Energy peer set of nine private and one public company (Lonza, LNZA), including later-stage comparables such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. A narrow peer-median approach was not feasible; no same-stage or adjacent-stage Climate & Energy companies with sufficient data density were available to support a reliable comparable valuation.

The analysis applies stage-progression methodology, which uses a 2.0x step-up multiplier applied to the $18M total raised as a proxy for current implied post-money valuation. This method assumes typical Series A-to-next-stage appreciation and yields an implied valuation of $36M. The peer-median approach was inapplicable due to insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) in narrowly filtered cohorts. Given single-method derivation, the triangulated range reflects a ±15% confidence band around the median: $31M (low), $36M (median), and $41M (high).

Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the stage-progression multiplier for this specific sector and the company's commercial trajectory relative to later-stage comparables. Validation would benefit from revenue or unit economics data and closer inspection of capital efficiency across the Climate & Energy peer set.
